posts.name: Username
posts.cooked:
Shadowvixyn:

I guess gaming via controller bridges the gap enough?

It does, for me. Everyone’s needs may be different.

This is what I use:

Controller: SCUF Envision Pro V2 with Hall Effect sticks
Pedal: Kinesis Savant Elite2 Dual Pedal FP20A

My left-side pedal is Push To Talk. The right-side heel pedal handles the repeated Single-Button Assistant press, while the controller provides distinct, comfortable manual binds for the spells the assistant skips, plus defensives, interrupt, movement and utility.

SCUF side buttons|commonly woven off-rotation damage abilities
SCUF G-keys|cooldowns, cleanse/dispel, crowd control, utility
Face buttons/triggers|movement, jump, targeting, modifiers or core combat navigation

So, essentially I have moved the highest-frequency, lowest-precision action - advancing the core damage rotation - to my foot, while keeping the cognitively important and fiddly actions in my hands: interrupts, defensives, movement abilities, cooldowns, target swaps and situational utility. When I healed PvP a lot a 3rd pedal would toggle me in and out of travel form as the situation required.

Many players use One-Button mapped to a key. But for me, putting it on one key concentrates too much repetitive work in one finger. If instead you put One-Button on a foot pedal its just like tapping your heel/foot to a song - can do that almost endlessly without strain. For a healing session I have specific songs picked out that map to the cadence of a resto druid. It helps me count (without counting).

For other classes and roles the rhythm is different so you’d need different tunes for your toons.
